sections.h2: Quick ways for a Balch Springs owner to sell
sections.html:
An owner here can list the house, find a buyer without an agent, or take a cash bid from someone who accepts the present condition and closes on your timetable. The best choice turns on the house's condition, any liens or city notices attached to it, and how soon you need the money.

Balch Springs is a city of owners: 64.7 percent of homes are occupied by the people who own them, and the average household has 3.29 people. Many sales involve family homes held for decades, houses that passed through an estate, or rentals a landlord is tired of managing. Most houses date from the postwar years, when the town grew as a commuter suburb of Dallas, so age-related repairs are common.

  • Market listing: works when the house shows well and a lender approves the buyer.
  • Investor purchase: no showings, no loan approval, and usually no repair list.
  • Payoffs first: a mortgage, tax balance or code fine comes out of the proceeds, so get each figure in writing before you accept anything.

A typical owned home was valued at $224,400 in the 2020-2024 estimates, and a typical renter paid $1,378 a month. The mid-2025 population estimate is 27,258, which is 1.6 percent under the 27,705 baseline for April 2020 but well above the 23,728 counted in 2010.

Ask the county appraisal district which school district taxes your parcel, because the town once split between the Dallas and Mesquite districts.

sections.h2: Rental registration and certificate of occupancy
sections.html:
Balch Springs requires both. A seller with a tenant, or an investor buyer, should expect to deal with each.

  • Rental registration: the applicant needs a driver's license and proof of ownership, such as closing paperwork or a deed in the applicant's name. The registration must be renewed every two years.
  • Inspection timing: rental inspections must be done before a tenant moves in, or the owner incurs a violation fee.
  • Certificate of occupancy: the applicant provides a driver's license, a lease or proof of ownership, a site map and a floor plan.

Registration is tied to the owner's name and deed. An investor who keeps the tenant therefore files a new registration once the deed is recorded. Call Permits and Inspections at 972-286-4477 to find out what is on file for your address. Inspection requests go by email to inspections@balchspringstx.gov, and the city's permits page has the forms.

sections.h2: Permits and sign-offs when a house changes hands
sections.html:
The permit sheet shows what a seller or investor buyer may need. Electrical, plumbing and air conditioning work each need their own permit, pulled by a registered master contractor. Roof work can be a same-day permit when no structural work is involved. Current codes are the 2021 IRC and IBC and the 2020 NEC.

If you are running an estate or moving sale, note the garage sale rules: three sales a calendar year, with 90 days between them. Contractors working on the house must be registered with the city, so confirm that anyone you hire for pre-sale repairs is on the list. Permits and Inspections can be reached at 972-286-4477.

sections.h2: Can an open city notice get in the way of a sale?
sections.html:
An open notice does not bar a sale, but it stays with the property and ought to be cleared or discussed before closing. Officers walk the neighborhoods every day and also act on complaints.

The first letter allows 10 days to fix the problem, shortened to 7 days for tall grass and solid waste, and it stays active for 12 months. If a return visit finds no change, the officer writes a Notice to Appear that names the ordinance, the fine and how to reach the court. Owners can ask the department for more time to finish a repair.

Before you list, walk the lot with the city's Top 10 violations list, which the Code Enforcement page offers in English and Spanish. Tell the buyer about any citation or court date so the closing is not held up.

sections.h2: Time left before a foreclosure auction
sections.html:
Most Texas home loans can be foreclosed without a lawsuit, and the calendar is firm enough that selling first is often workable. Federal servicing rules generally hold off a first filing until the loan is over 120 days delinquent.

  • A borrower can reinstate by paying what is past due within 20 days after the default notice arrives.
  • The servicer then sends a sale notice at least 21 days ahead, posts it at the courthouse and files it with the county clerk.
  • Auctions are held on the first Tuesday of the month, between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m.
  • A lender can sue for a shortfall within two years, and the borrower can ask for a credit for the home's fair market value.

The Dallas County commissioners court sets the auction location, so ask the county clerk where it is. A sale that closes before the first Tuesday can pay off the loan from the proceeds. The State Law Library's foreclosure guide walks through each stage.

sections.h2: How a tenant changes the sale
sections.html:
Give every buyer a copy of the lease, because its terms govern what a new owner can do about the occupant. If you need the tenant out before closing, a written notice to vacate normally allows at least three days unless the lease sets another period.

An eviction suit goes to justice court. The tenant must be served four days or more before trial, and a hearing is set 10 to 21 days after filing. A losing party can appeal to county court within five days, and a writ of possession waits at least six days after final judgment. Many owners with tenants simply choose a buyer who will keep the tenant, which skips that timeline.

sections.h2: Filing the deed and finishing the sale
sections.html: The deed is filed with the Dallas County clerk, since the city lies in Dallas County. It must be signed and acknowledged before a notary or other authorized officer. Once funds are in, the title company sends the deed for recording and pays off each lien from your proceeds. Keep the settlement statement and any payoff receipts for your records.

faqs.q: Must I keep my rental registered until the Balch Springs sale closes?
faqs.a: Yes, while the house is rented. The registration lasts two years and requires an inspection before a tenant moves in. A buyer who keeps renting registers in their own name with proof of ownership.

faqs.q: How soon must a Balch Springs code notice be fixed?
faqs.a: Ten days for most notices and seven days for tall grass or solid waste. If a return inspection still finds the problem, a citation with a fine and court date follows. You may ask for more time.

faqs.q: Where is the deed filed for a Balch Springs sale?
faqs.a: With the Dallas County clerk, since the city lies in Dallas County. The deed must be signed and acknowledged before a notary or other authorized officer.

faqs.q: Is it too late to sell once the lender posts a foreclosure notice?
faqs.a: Not if the sale closes first. The borrower has 20 days from the default notice to reinstate, and the lender owes at least 21 days' notice of sale. Count back from the first Tuesday of the month.

faqs.q: How many people live in Balch Springs?
faqs.a: An estimated 27,258 as of July 2025, with 8,247 households counted in 2020-2024. That is 1.6 percent below the April 2020 baseline, across 9.02 square miles.
